tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", do neither.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

## 672a8514-c737-4d94-90c2-4764adea0010
This is an MCP server provided by Gmail API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Gmail.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application. Finder is an application like any other: clicking the desktop, the Dock, or a Finder window (including Go to Folder) requires a Finder grant. The menu bar does not, as long as the app that is frontmost is one you have at tier "full".

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, drag-drop, and the menu bar are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool. Never use it, AppleScript or other scripting to get around these limits.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.

#!/usr/bin/env node
// Operation ASCEND B2.9: compare the protected canonical environment with a release environment for the switches that
// decide live recruitment, retention and automation behaviour. Prints key names and a verdict only, never a value.
//
// Usage: node scripts/check-release-env-drift.mjs <canonical .env> <release .env>
// Exit 0 when every governed switch is present and identical in both files; 1 otherwise; 2 on usage errors.
//
// Why: on 24 November 2026 the live release environment carried the approved B2.9 switches while the canonical checkout's
// .env did not. A release built or restarted from the canonical file would have silently switched recruitment and the
// ASCEND engine back to their code defaults. This check makes that drift a release blocker.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { parseEnv } from "node:util"
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"

/** Switches whose value is a founder decision. Secrets are deliberately excluded: they are compared by presence only. */
export const GOVERNED_SWITCHES = Object.freeze([
  "PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED", "PARTNER_APPLICATION_PRIVACY_VERSION", "PARTNER_APPLICATION_RETENTION_DAYS", "PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED",
  "EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED",
  "ASCEND_ENGINE_ENABLED", "ASCEND_SCHEDULER_ENABLED", "ASCEND_AGENT_API_ENABLED", "ASCEND_AUTOMATION_ENABLED",
  "MEGATON_ENABLED", "MEGATON_STOP", "MEGATON_EXTERNAL_ENABLED", "MEGATON_WORKER_SEND_ENABLED", "MEGATON_SEND_ENABLED", "MEGATON_SOCIAL_SEND_ENABLED",
  "MEGATON_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED", "MEGATON_MESSAGE_RETENTION_DAYS",
])

/** Returns one entry per governed switch: identical, differs, missing_in_canonical, missing_in_release or absent_in_both. */
export function compareEnvironments(canonicalText, releaseText, keys = GOVERNED_SWITCHES) {
  const canonical = parseEnv(canonicalText), release = parseEnv(releaseText)
  return keys.map((key) => {
    const inC = Object.hasOwn(canonical, key), inR = Object.hasOwn(release, key)
    const status = !inC && !inR ? "absent_in_both" : !inC ? "missing_in_canonical" : !inR ? "missing_in_release" : canonical[key] === release[key] ? "identical" : "differs"
    return { key, status }
  })
}

/** Absent in both is acceptable (code default applies equally); anything else is drift. */
export const isDrift = (entry) => entry.status !== "identical" && entry.status !== "absent_in_both"

if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1] ?? "").href) {
  const [canonicalPath, releasePath] = process.argv.slice(2)
  if (!canonicalPath || !releasePath) { console.error("Usage: node scripts/check-release-env-drift.mjs <canonical .env> <release .env>"); process.exit(2) }
  const result = compareEnvironments(readFileSync(canonicalPath, "utf8"), readFileSync(releasePath, "utf8"))
  for (const r of result) console.log(`${isDrift(r) ? "DRIFT" : "ok   "} ${r.key.padEnd(38)} ${r.status}`)
  const drift = result.filter(isDrift).length
  console.log(drift ? `\nBLOCKED: ${drift} governed switch(es) differ between the canonical and release environments (values not shown).` : "\nNo drift in governed switches.")
  process.exitCode = drift ? 1 : 0
}
----
# X requires a user-context token; Facebook requires Page access, not personal profiles.
MEGATON_SOCIAL_SEND_ENABLED=false
MEGATON_X_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN=
MEGATON_FACEBOOK_PAGE_TOKEN=
MEGATON_FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID=
MEGATON_FACEBOOK_API_VERSION=

# Operation Expansion: public intake stays closed until privacy and operations approval.
# Existing Auth.js identity/session configuration is reused for the /partner portal.
PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED=false
PARTNER_APPLICATION_PRIVACY_VERSION=
# Choose a reviewed applicant retention period (1..730 days) before enabling intake.
PARTNER_APPLICATION_RETENTION_DAYS=
# Enable founder-confirmed terminal applicant cleanup only after retention policy approval.
PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false
# Enable new invitations and activation only after separate commercial pilot approval.
PARTNER_ACTIVATION_ENABLED=false
# Personal partner webpages. Both switches stay off until founder, legal and privacy approval of the consent text, privacy notice and publication.
# Admin app: allows a founder to publish an approved profile version. Approving wording never publishes it.
PARTNER_PROFILE_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=false
# Web app: serves /partners/[slug]. When unset or not "true" the route returns 404 for every slug.
PUBLIC_PARTNER_PROFILES_ENABLED=false
# Operation Empower (B1). Admin app: founder Content workspace for drafting, reviewing, approving and publishing partner content.
# Nothing is served to partners by this switch; partner Resource Centre and Academy have their own switches in later phases.
EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED=false
# Operation Empower B1.2. Admin app: the partner Academy (/partner/academy). Independent of the founder switch above; serves only
# courses and lessons a founder has approved and published, still inside their review date. Keep off until content is approved.
PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED=false
# Operation Empower B1.3. Admin app: the partner Resource Centre (/partner/resources): approved resources, search and downloads.
# Independent of the switches above; serves only resources a founder has approved and published, inside their review date.
PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED=false
# Operation Empower B1.4. Admin app: the partner Knowledge Base (/partner/knowledge): approved answers to client questions.
# Independent of the switches above; serves only entries a founder has approved and published, inside their review date.
PARTNER_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ENABLED=false
# Operation Launch Ready. Web and admin: partner lifecycle email (application received, information requested, declined,
# invitation, activation, updated agreement) through Resend (RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM). Off by default; every attempt is
# logged in partner_notifications with a hash of the recipient, and founders see the outcome. Turn on only after the sending
# domain is verified and the wording is approved.
PARTNER_EMAIL_ENABLED=false
# Optional reply-to address for partner email, so applicants' replies reach a monitored founder inbox.
PARTNER_EMAIL_REPLY_TO=
# Operation Empower B1.5. Admin app: partner objection handling (/partner/objections): founder-approved responses to client objections,
# with client-safe wording, discovery questions, limitations, escalation and related material. Independent of the switches above;
# serves only partner-only objection responses a founder has approved and published, inside their review date.
PARTNER_OBJECTION_HANDLING_ENABLED=false
# Operation Empower B1.6. Admin app: the unified partner workspace: a "Today" overview, contextual guidance on each prospect,
# meeting preparation and one search across approved answers, resources and learning (/partner/guidance). Read-only over existing
# records; each module still needs its own switch. Off by default.
PARTNER_UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_ENABLED=false
# Operation Ascend B2.1. Admin app: the partner pipeline (/partner/pipeline): board, table and list of the partner's own
# opportunities, a partner-safe history, an append-only interaction log and private follow-up dates. Stage changes still go
# through the existing authorised commands. Needs migration 0098. Off by default.
PARTNER_PIPELINE_ENABLED=false
# Operation Ascend B2.2. Admin app: qualification readiness inside the pipeline (partners) and on each opportunity (founders):
# an explainable checklist over recorded discovery answers. Display only; it never rejects a prospect or changes any rule. Off by default.
PARTNER_QUALIFICATION_ENABLED=false
# Operation Ascend B2.3. Admin app: the founder sales command centre (/expansion/command): pipeline overview, a prioritised work queue
# linked to where each item is decided, partner oversight and internal founder assignment (needs migration 0100). Off by default.
FOUNDER_SALES_COMMAND_ENABLED=false
# Operation Ascend B2.4. Admin app: revenue intelligence (/expansion/revenue) for founders with finance access: actual revenue and
# commission from the authoritative records, and hypothetical forecasts from versioned assumptions (needs migration 0101). Off by default.
REVENUE_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED=false

# Operation Ascend B2.6: reviewed sales-to-delivery handoffs (default off)
DELIVERY_HANDOFF_ENABLED=false
# B2.7 read-only operational signals, requires founder command and B2.6 handoff flags
ASCEND_AUTOMATION_ENABLED=false
# B2.8 execution engine (admin). Off by default. Even when on, automation starts under a global emergency stop and every
# definition starts disabled; founders resume and enable deliberately in /expansion/automation/engine.
ASCEND_ENGINE_ENABLED=false
# Unattended interval scheduling. Keep off until scheduling has been verified and authorised.
ASCEND_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false
# TITAN OS / Jarvis agent interface (/api/ascend/v1/*). Keep off until an agent identity is authorised.
ASCEND_AGENT_API_ENABLED=false
# Total executions leased at once across all workers (1-32).
ASCEND_MAX_GLOBAL_CONCURRENCY=4
# ASCEND worker process (ops/ascend/ascend-worker.mjs), run under PM2 beside the admin app. Token issued once in the
# command centre; never commit it. URL must be loopback HTTP or HTTPS.
ASCEND_WORKER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3301/api/ascend/worker
ASCEND_WORKER_TOKEN=
ASCEND_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=1

# Operation ASCEND B2.5: own performance dashboard (off until founder-authorised pilot)
PARTNER_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED=false

**Interpretation.** Read paths (overview, explorer) match B2.8 at every scale, and claim latency stays flat as history
grows 500-fold, so indexes behave as before. Write-path numbers are 30–60× worse because this host's durable commit is
1. **Canonical checkout is behind master.** `/var/www/scalesmiths/ScaleSmiths` is on branch `chore/ascend-worker-preflight-20261123`
   at `2460de1` (four VPS-only commits `b7282d7`, `d0e153f`, `4814408`, `2460de1`). Every line it has that master lacks is an
   older version of code master superseded (the first Megaton preflight and pre-B2.8 files); master contains the
   recovered commits' content via #177. Two untracked paths (`admin/node`, `admin/scalesmiths-admin@0.1.0`) are stray
   npm artefacts. **Nothing in the checkout is unrecovered work.** Moving it to master is a production change left for a founder.
2. **Configuration drift (release blocker for future deploys).** `scripts/check-release-env-drift.mjs` (new in B2.9) run
   against the two files: 8 governed switches exist in the live release `.env` but are **missing from the canonical
   `.env`**: `PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED`, `PARTNER_APPLICATION_PRIVACY_VERSION`, `PARTNER_APPLICATION_RETENTION_DAYS`,
   `PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED`, `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED`, `ASCEND_ENGINE_ENABLED`, `ASCEND_SCHEDULER_ENABLED`,
   `ASCEND_AGENT_API_ENABLED`. A release prepared from the canonical file would switch public recruitment off. All Megaton
   switches are identical in both files.
3. **Stale canary processes still online.** PM2 `scalesmiths-web-canary` and `scalesmiths-admin-canary` run release
   `e48967b` on 127.0.0.1:3200/3201. Nginx does not route to them, but they hold database connections and run code older
   than migration 0104 against the migrated database.
4. **Machine routes are reachable from the public hosts.** Nginx proxies every path of `partners.` and `admin.scalesmiths.co.uk`
   to :3301, including `/api/ascend/worker` and `/api/megaton/worker`. Both authenticate (observed: worker 401,
   capabilities 404), but the worker is designed to use loopback only, so public exposure is unnecessary attack surface.
5. **Megaton worker crash history.** `scalesmiths-megaton-worker` is `stopped`, `autorestart=true`, cwd release `6dcfeff`,
   with **2,878,404 recorded restarts**. If anyone runs `pm2 restart all` or `pm2 resurrect`, it starts on a stale release.
6. **The live b257 processes carry no `SS_RELEASE_ID`** in their PM2 environment; health reports the release from the
   build. Harmless, but the PM2 listing cannot be used to confirm release identity.

## Live switches (non-secret values)

Live release `.env`: `PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED=true`, `REDACTED`,
`PARTNER_APPLICATION_RETENTION_DAYS=180`, `PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false`, `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED=true`,
`ASCEND_ENGINE_ENABLED=true`, `ASCEND_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false`, `ASCEND_AGENT_API_ENABLED=false`, `ASCEND_AUTOMATION_ENABLED` unset.
Megaton: `MEGATON_ENABLED=true`, `MEGATON_STOP=false`, `MEGATON_EXTERNAL_ENABLED=true`, `MEGATON_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED=true`,
all send switches `false`, `MEGATON_MESSAGE_RETENTION_DAYS=0`. Both `.env` files: mode `600 root:root`, regular files.

## Processes and routing

| PM2 process | Status | Restarts | Release | Port |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| scalesmiths-web-b257 | online | 0 | f55a6bc | 3300 (nginx `scalesmiths.co.uk`) |
| scalesmiths-admin-b257 | online | 0 | f55a6bc | 3301 (nginx `admin.` and `partners.`) |
| scalesmiths-web-canary | online | 0 | e48967b | 3200 (not routed) |
| scalesmiths-admin-canary | online | 0 | e48967b | 3201 (not routed) |
| scalesmiths-megaton-worker | stopped | 2,878,404 | 6dcfeff | n/a |

All processes run as `root`; no `max_memory_restart` is set on any of them.

16	 * supersede and withdraw content. Nothing here serves content to partners: `servableContent` is the single read rule later phases
17	 * must use, and it is exercised only by tests until a partner surface ships behind its own switch.
18	 * The whole workspace is OFF unless EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED=true.
19	 * Lock order: admin_users (share) -> empower_content_items (update) -> empower_content_versions (update).
20	 */
21	type Row = Record<string, unknown>
22	type Executor = Pick<AdminDatabaseTransaction, "execute">
23	type Actor = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof requireCapability>>
24	const FOUNDER_ROLES = ADMIN_ROLES.filter((role) => hasCapability(role, "expansion.manage"))
25	
26	export const founderContentEnabled = () => process.env.EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED === "true"
27	const rows = async (tx: Executor, query: SQL): Promise<Row[]> => (await tx.execute(query)).rows as Row[]
28	const uuid = (value: unknown) => {
29	  if (typeof value !== "string" || !/^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i.test(value)) throw new ContentError("A valid record identifier is required.")
30	  return value.toLowerCase()
31	}
32	const conflict = (message: string): never => { throw new ContentError(message, 409) }
33	const audit = (tx: Executor, actorId: string, entity: string, action: string, details: unknown) =>
34	  tx.execute(sql`insert into expansion_audit(actor_id,entity_id,action,details) values(${actorId},${entity},${action},${JSON.stringify(details)}::jsonb)`)
35	/** Database refusals (lifecycle trigger, unique indexes) become founder-readable conflicts; anything else propagates. */
36	async function guarded<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>, fallback: string): Promise<T> {
37	  try { return await operation() } catch (error) {
38	    if (error instanceof ContentError) throw error
39	    const safe = translateDbError(error, fallback)
40	    if (safe) throw new ContentError(safe.message, safe.status)
41	    throw error
42	  }
43	}
44	
45	async function founder() {
46	  if (!founderContentEnabled()) throw new ContentError("The founder Content workspace is not enabled in this environment.", 404)
47	  return requireCapability("expansion.manage")
48	}
49	async function founderGuard(tx: Executor, actor: Actor) {
50	  const [user] = await rows(tx, sql`select role::text,active,session_version from admin_users where id=${actor.id} for share`)
51	  if (!user?.active || user.session_version !== actor.sessionVersion || !hasCapability(user.role as AdminRole, "expansion.manage")) throw new ContentError("Founder authority was revoked.", 403)
52	}
53	async function activeFounderCount(tx: Executor) {
54	  const roleList = sql.join(FOUNDER_ROLES.map((role) => sql`${role}`), sql`,`)
55	  // Share-locked so a founder cannot self-approve while a second founder is being activated concurrently (AP-GOV-04).
56	  const [row] = await rows(tx, sql`select count(*)::int n from (select id from admin_users where active=true and role::text in (${roleList}) for share) founders`)
57	  return Number(row.n)
58	}
59	async function lockVersion(tx: Executor, id: string) {
60	  const [src] = await rows(tx, sql`select item_id from empower_content_versions where id=${id}`)
61	  if (!src) throw new ContentError("Content version not found.", 404)
62	  const [item] = await rows(tx, sql`select * from empower_content_items where id=${String(src.item_id)} for update`)
63	  const [version] = await rows(tx, sql`select * from empower_content_versions where id=${id} for update`)
64	  return { item, version }
65	}
66	
67	/**
68	 * AP-GOV-04 separation of duties: a version has exactly one author, who alone may edit and submit it. Otherwise a second founder
69	 * could rewrite someone else's draft and then approve it as "not the author". Another founder can archive an abandoned draft
70	 * and start their own revision instead.
71	 */
72	function requireAuthor(version: Row, actor: Actor) {
73	  if (String(version.created_by) !== actor.id) throw new ContentError("Only the author of this draft can edit or submit it. Archive it and start your own revision instead.", 403)
74	}
75	
76	/**
77	 * B1.2: a course may be submitted or published only when every linked lesson has a published, in-date version. Lessons are
78	 * approved independently (with their own author/approver separation), so a founder cannot slip their own unreviewed lesson
79	 * into a course. Lesson item rows are share-locked in id order so a concurrent withdrawal waits for this check.
80	 */
81	async function assertCourseLessonsServable(tx: Executor, fields: unknown) {
82	  const ids = courseLessonIds(fields)
83	  if (!ids.length) throw new ContentError("A course needs at least one lesson.", 409)
84	  const list = sql.join(ids.map((lessonId) => sql`${lessonId}::uuid`), sql`,`)
85	  await tx.execute(sql`select id from empower_content_items where id in (${list}) order by id for share`)
86	  const ready = await rows(tx, sql`select i.id from empower_content_items i join empower_content_versions v on v.item_id=i.id and v.status='published' and v.review_by >= (now() at time zone 'UTC')::date where i.kind='lesson' and i.audience='partner_only' and i.id in (${list})`)
87	  const missing = ids.filter((lessonId) => !ready.some((r) => String(r.id) === lessonId))
88	  if (missing.length) throw new ContentError(`Every lesson in a course must be a published, in-date, partner-only lesson first (${missing.length} of ${ids.length} not ready).`, 409)
89	}
90	
91	export interface DraftInput { title?: unknown; body?: unknown; fields?: unknown; sourceRefs?: unknown; changeSummary?: unknown }
92	function draftValues(kind: ContentKind, input: DraftInput) {
93	  return {
94	    title: contentTitle(input.title), body: contentBody(input.body ?? ""), fields: contentFields(kind, input.fields, false),
95	    sources: sourceRefs(input.sourceRefs), summary: changeSummary(input.changeSummary),
96	  }
97	}
98	
99	export async function createContentItem(input: DraftInput & { kind?: unknown; slug?: unknown; audience?: unknown; cadence?: unknown }) {
100	  const actor = await founder()
101	  const kind = contentKind(input.kind), slug = contentSlug(input.slug), audience = contentAudience(input.audience), cadence = reviewCadence(input.cadence)
102	  if (kind === "course" && audience !== "partner_only") throw new ContentError("Academy courses are for partners only.")
103	  if (kind === "agreement" && (audience !== "partner_only" || cadence !== 3)) throw new ContentError("Partner agreements are partner-only and reviewed on the commercial (3-month) cadence.")
104	  const values = draftValues(kind, input)
105	  const itemId = randomUUID(), versionId = randomUUID()
106	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
107	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
108	    await tx.execute(sql`insert into empower_content_items(id,kind,slug,audience,review_cadence_months,created_by) values(${itemId},${kind},${slug},${audience},${cadence},${actor.id})`)
109	    await tx.execute(sql`insert into empower_content_versions(id,item_id,version,title,body,fields,source_refs,change_summary,created_by)
110	      values(${versionId},${itemId},1,${values.title},${values.body},${JSON.stringify(values.fields)}::jsonb,${JSON.stringify(values.sources)}::jsonb,${values.summary},${actor.id})`)
111	    await audit(tx, actor.id, itemId, "empower_item_created", { kind, slug, audience, reviewCadenceMonths: cadence, versionId })
112	    return { itemId, versionId, version: 1 }
113	  }, "A content item with that slug already exists."))
114	}
115	
116	export async function saveContentDraft(input: DraftInput & { versionId?: unknown }) {
117	  const actor = await founder(), id = uuid(input.versionId)
118	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
119	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
120	    const { item, version } = await lockVersion(tx, id)
121	    if (version.status !== "draft") conflict("Only a draft can be edited. Start a new revision instead.")
122	    requireAuthor(version, actor)
123	    const values = draftValues(item.kind as ContentKind, input)
124	    await tx.execute(sql`update empower_content_versions set title=${values.title},body=${values.body},fields=${JSON.stringify(values.fields)}::jsonb,
125	      source_refs=${JSON.stringify(values.sources)}::jsonb,change_summary=${values.summary} where id=${id}`)
126	    await audit(tx, actor.id, id, "empower_draft_saved", { itemId: item.id, version: version.version })
127	    return { versionId: id }
128	  }, "This draft cannot be saved."))
129	}
130	
131	/** Starts the next version of an item from its latest content. Only one version may be in progress at a time. */
132	export async function startContentRevision(input: { itemId?: unknown; changeSummary?: unknown }) {
133	  const actor = await founder(), itemId = uuid(input.itemId), summary = changeSummary(input.changeSummary)
134	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
135	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
136	    const [item] = await rows(tx, sql`select * from empower_content_items where id=${itemId} for update`)
137	    if (!item) throw new ContentError("Content item not found.", 404)
138	    const [open] = await rows(tx, sql`select id,status from empower_content_versions where item_id=${itemId} and status in ('draft','in_review','approved')`)
139	    if (open) conflict(`Version in progress (${String(open.status).replace("_", " ")}): finish or archive it first.`)
140	    const [latest] = await rows(tx, sql`select * from empower_content_versions where item_id=${itemId} order by version desc limit 1`)
141	    const versionId = randomUUID(), next = Number(latest.version) + 1
142	    await tx.execute(sql`insert into empower_content_versions(id,item_id,version,title,body,fields,source_refs,change_summary,created_by)
143	      values(${versionId},${itemId},${next},${String(latest.title)},${String(latest.body)},${JSON.stringify(latest.fields)}::jsonb,${JSON.stringify(latest.source_refs)}::jsonb,${summary},${actor.id})`)
144	    await audit(tx, actor.id, versionId, "empower_revision_started", { itemId, version: next, fromVersion: latest.version })
145	    return { versionId, version: next }
146	  }, "A revision could not be started."))
147	}
148	
149	export async function submitContentVersion(input: { versionId?: unknown; lintOverrideReason?: unknown }) {
150	  const actor = await founder(), id = uuid(input.versionId)
151	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
152	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
153	    const { item, version } = await lockVersion(tx, id)
154	    if (version.status !== "draft") conflict("Only a draft can be submitted for review.")
155	    requireAuthor(version, actor)
156	    const check = checkSubmission({
157	      kind: item.kind as ContentKind, audience: item.audience as ContentAudience, cadenceMonths: Number(item.review_cadence_months),
158	      title: String(version.title), body: String(version.body), fields: version.fields, sources: version.source_refs, lintOverrideReason: input.lintOverrideReason,
159	    })
160	    await tx.execute(sql`update empower_content_versions set lint_override_reason=${check.lintOverrideReason} where id=${id}`)
161	    if (item.kind === "course") await assertCourseLessonsServable(tx, check.fields)
162	    await tx.execute(sql`update empower_content_versions set status='in_review',submitted_by=${actor.id},submitted_at=now() where id=${id}`)
163	    await audit(tx, actor.id, id, "empower_submitted", { itemId: item.id, version: version.version, lintHits: check.lintHits, lintOverridden: Boolean(check.lintOverrideReason) })
164	    return { versionId: id, status: "in_review" }
165	  }, "This version cannot be submitted."))
166	}
167	
168	export async function decideContentVersion(input: { versionId?: unknown; decision?: unknown; reference?: unknown; notes?: unknown; reviewBy?: unknown; selfApprovalReason?: unknown }) {
169	  const actor = await founder(), id = uuid(input.versionId), decision = contentDecision(input.decision)
170	  const reference = typeof input.reference === "string" ? input.reference.trim() : ""
171	  const notes = typeof input.notes === "string" ? input.notes.trim() : ""
172	  if (reference.length < 3 || reference.length > 200) throw new ContentError("Record the decision reference (3 to 200 characters).")
173	  if (notes.length < 5 || notes.length > 2000) throw new ContentError("Record the reason for your decision (5 to 2000 characters).")
174	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
175	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
176	    const { item, version } = await lockVersion(tx, id)
177	    if (version.status !== "in_review") conflict("Only a version in review can receive a decision.")
178	    let reviewBy: string | null = null, selfApprovalReason: string | null = null
179	    if (decision === "approved") {
180	      reviewBy = reviewByDate(input.reviewBy, Number(item.review_cadence_months))
181	      selfApprovalReason = approvalAuthority({ approverId: actor.id, authorId: String(version.created_by), activeFounders: await activeFounderCount(tx), selfApprovalReason: input.selfApprovalReason }).selfApprovalReason
182	    } else if (input.selfApprovalReason) throw new ContentError("A self-approval reason applies only to approval.")
183	    const approvalId = randomUUID()
184	    await tx.execute(sql`insert into empower_content_approvals(id,version_id,decision,decided_by,reference,notes,review_by,self_approval_reason)
185	      values(${approvalId},${id},${decision},${actor.id},${reference},${notes},${reviewBy},${selfApprovalReason})`)
186	    if (decision === "approved") await tx.execute(sql`update empower_content_versions set status='approved',review_by=${reviewBy},approved_at=now() where id=${id}`)
187	    else if (decision === "changes_requested") await tx.execute(sql`update empower_content_versions set status='changes_requested' where id=${id}`)
188	    else await tx.execute(sql`update empower_content_versions set status='archived',archived_at=now(),archive_reason=${`Rejected: ${notes}`.slice(0, 2000)} where id=${id}`)
189	    await audit(tx, actor.id, id, `empower_${decision}`, { itemId: item.id, version: version.version, approvalId, reference, reviewBy, selfApproval: Boolean(selfApprovalReason) })
190	    return { versionId: id, status: decision === "rejected" ? "archived" : decision, approvalId }
191	  }, "This decision is not permitted."))
192	}
193	
194	/** Publishing a version supersedes the item's previously published version in the same transaction. */
195	export async function publishContentVersion(input: { versionId?: unknown }) {
196	  const actor = await founder(), id = uuid(input.versionId)
197	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
198	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
199	    const { item, version } = await lockVersion(tx, id)
200	    if (version.status !== "approved") conflict("Only an approved version can be published.")
201	    // A course is published only if every lesson it links is itself published and in date at this moment (lesson rows share-locked).
202	    if (item.kind === "course") await assertCourseLessonsServable(tx, version.fields)
203	    const superseded = await rows(tx, sql`update empower_content_versions set status='superseded',superseded_at=now() where item_id=${String(item.id)} and status='published' returning id,version`)
204	    await tx.execute(sql`update empower_content_versions set status='published',published_at=now() where id=${id}`)
205	    await audit(tx, actor.id, id, "empower_published", { itemId: item.id, version: version.version, supersededVersionIds: superseded.map((r) => r.id) })
206	    return { versionId: id, status: "published", superseded: superseded.map((r) => Number(r.version)) }
207	  }, "This version cannot be published."))
208	}
209	
210	/** Archives a draft or approved version, or withdraws a published one (reason required, AP-PUB-01). History is kept. */
211	export async function archiveContentVersion(input: { versionId?: unknown; reason?: unknown }) {
212	  const actor = await founder(), id = uuid(input.versionId)
213	  const reason = typeof input.reason === "string" ? input.reason.trim() : ""
214	  if (reason.length < 5 || reason.length > 2000) throw new ContentError("Record the reason (5 to 2000 characters).")
215	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
216	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
217	    const { item, version } = await lockVersion(tx, id)
218	    if (!["draft", "approved", "published"].includes(String(version.status))) conflict("This version cannot be archived from its current state.")
219	    await tx.execute(sql`update empower_content_versions set status='archived',archived_at=now(),archive_reason=${reason} where id=${id}`)
220	    await audit(tx, actor.id, id, version.status === "published" ? "empower_withdrawn" : "empower_archived", { itemId: item.id, version: version.version, reason })
221	    return { versionId: id, status: "archived" }
222	  }, "This version cannot be archived."))
223	}
224	
225	/**
226	 * THE read rule for any partner-facing surface: published, inside its review window, and in an audience the reader may see.
227	 * Everything else (drafts, in review, approved-but-unpublished, superseded, archived, expired) is never returned.
228	 */
229	export async function servableContent(tx: Executor, audiences: readonly ContentAudience[], options: { kind?: ContentKind; asOf?: string } = {}) {
230	  if (!audiences.length) return []
231	  const list = sql.join(audiences.map((a) => sql`${contentAudience(a)}`), sql`,`)
232	  const { kind } = options
233	  // UTC calendar date, matching the database guards. `asOf` exists only so tests can check expiry deterministically.
234	  if (options.asOf !== undefined && !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(options.asOf)) throw new ContentError("Invalid date.")
235	  const today = options.asOf ? sql`${options.asOf}::date` : sql`(now() at time zone 'UTC')::date`
236	  return rows(tx, sql`select i.id item_id,i.slug,i.kind,i.audience,v.id version_id,v.version,v.title,v.body,v.fields,v.source_refs,v.approved_at,v.review_by,v.published_at
237	    from empower_content_versions v join empower_content_items i on i.id=v.item_id
238	    where v.status='published' and v.review_by >= ${today} and i.audience in (${list}) ${kind ? sql`and i.kind=${contentKind(kind)}` : sql`and i.kind<>'agreement'`}
239	    order by i.kind, i.slug`)
240	}
241	
242	export async function getContentAdmin() {
243	  if (!founderContentEnabled()) return { enabled: false }
244	  const actor = await requireCapability("expansion.manage")
245	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
246	    await tx.execute(sql`set transaction isolation level repeatable read`)
247	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
248	    const items = await rows(tx, sql`select i.id,i.kind,i.slug,i.audience,i.review_cadence_months,i.created_at,u.display_name created_by_name from empower_content_items i join admin_users u on u.id=i.created_by order by i.kind,i.slug`)
249	    const versions = await rows(tx, sql`select v.id,v.item_id,v.version,v.title,v.body,v.fields,v.source_refs,v.change_summary,v.lint_override_reason,v.status,v.review_by,v.approved_at,v.published_at,
250	      v.superseded_at,v.archived_at,v.archive_reason,v.submitted_at,v.created_at,v.created_by,u.display_name author_name,(v.status='published' and v.review_by < (now() at time zone 'UTC')::date) review_overdue
251	      from empower_content_versions v join admin_users u on u.id=v.created_by order by v.item_id,v.version desc`)
252	    const approvals = await rows(tx, sql`select a.id,a.version_id,a.decision,a.decided_at,a.reference,a.notes,a.review_by,a.self_approval_reason,u.display_name decided_by_name
253	      from empower_content_approvals a join admin_users u on u.id=a.decided_by order by a.decided_at desc`)
254	    const synonyms = await rows(tx, sql`select s.id,s.term,s.expansion,s.active,s.created_at,u.display_name created_by_name from empower_search_synonyms s join admin_users u on u.id=s.created_by order by s.active desc, s.term`)
255	    const counts: Record<string, number> = {}
256	    for (const v of versions) counts[String(v.status)] = (counts[String(v.status)] ?? 0) + 1
257	    return { enabled: true, items, versions, approvals, synonyms, counts, reviewDue: versions.filter((v) => v.review_overdue).length, activeFounders: await activeFounderCount(tx), actorId: actor.id }
258	  })
259	}
260	
261	/** B1.3: founder-managed search synonyms. A synonym is retired by switching it off; history is never rewritten or deleted. */
262	export async function addSearchSynonym(input: { term?: unknown; expansion?: unknown }) {
263	  const actor = await founder(), term = synonymTerm(input.term), expansion = synonymExpansion(input.expansion), id = randomUUID()
264	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
265	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
266	    await tx.execute(sql`insert into empower_search_synonyms(id,term,expansion,created_by) values(${id},${term},${expansion},${actor.id})`)
267	    await audit(tx, actor.id, id, "empower_synonym_added", { term, expansion })
268	    return { id, term, expansion }
269	  }, "An active synonym for that term already exists; switch it off first."))
270	}
271	export async function setSearchSynonymActive(input: { id?: unknown; active?: unknown }) {
272	  const actor = await founder(), id = uuid(input.id), active = input.active === true || input.active === "true"
273	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => guarded(async () => {
274	    await founderGuard(tx, actor)
275	    const updated = await rows(tx, sql`update empower_search_synonyms set active=${active},updated_by=${actor.id} where id=${id} returning term`)
276	    if (!updated.length) throw new ContentError("Synonym not found.", 404)
277	    await audit(tx, actor.id, id, active ? "empower_synonym_enabled" : "empower_synonym_disabled", { term: updated[0].term })
278	    return { id, active }
279	  }, "An active synonym for that term already exists."))
280	}

1	import "server-only"
2	import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto"
3	import { sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm"
4	import { db, type AdminDatabaseTransaction } from "@/lib/db"
5	import { translateDbError } from "@/lib/db-errors"
6	import { ContentError, courseLessonIds, gradeCheck, publicChecks, type CourseModule } from "@/lib/empower-content"
7	import { requireCapability } from "./rbac"
8	import { partnerAcademyEnabled, partnerGuard } from "./empower-partner"
9	import { relatedResourcesForLessons } from "./empower-resources"
10	export { partnerAcademyEnabled }
11	
12	/*
13	 * Operation Empower B1.2: the partner side of the Academy. OFF unless PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED=true, independently of the founder
14	 * studio switch. Every read goes through the published, in-date rule: a course is listed only while its current version is
15	 * published and in date, and a lesson inside it only while the lesson's own current version is too. Anything else is presented
16	 * as "temporarily unavailable" with no content (fail closed).
17	 *
18	 * Learning records are private to the partner who made them, keyed by the authenticated partner via `partnerGuard`, voluntary,
19	 * and never read by any commission, allocation, achievement, referral or withdrawal code. A completion belongs to the exact lesson
20	 * version read: when a lesson is revised, the earlier completion is kept and shown as "updated since you completed it", and the
21	 * new version is not claimed as complete.
22	 */
23	type Row = Record<string, unknown>
24	type Executor = Pick<AdminDatabaseTransaction, "execute">
25	
26	const rows = async (tx: Executor, query: SQL): Promise<Row[]> => (await tx.execute(query)).rows as Row[]
27	const uuidList = (ids: string[]) => sql.join(ids.map((id) => sql`${id}::uuid`), sql`,`)
28	const UTC_TODAY = sql`(now() at time zone 'UTC')::date`
29	const uuid = (value: unknown) => {
30	  if (typeof value !== "string" || !/^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i.test(value)) throw new ContentError("A valid record identifier is required.")
31	  return value.toLowerCase()
32	}
33	
34	async function partner() {
35	  if (!partnerAcademyEnabled()) throw new ContentError("The Partner Academy is not available yet.", 404)
36	  return requireCapability("expansion.partner")
37	}
38	
39	interface LessonView { itemId: string; available: boolean; versionId?: string; version?: number; slug?: string; title?: string; readingMinutes?: number | null; publishedAt?: string; state: "completed" | "updated" | "not_started" | "unavailable"; completedAt?: string | null; checks?: number }
40	interface CourseView { itemId: string; slug: string; versionId: string; version: number; title: string; description: string; category: string | null; objectives: string[]; estimatedMinutes: number | null; publishedAt: string; updatedAt: string; modules: { title: string; summary?: string; lessons: LessonView[] }[]; progress: { completed: number; available: number; unavailable: number }; lastLessonItemId: string | null; lastViewedAt: string | null }
41	
42	async function load(tx: Executor, partnerId: string, slug?: string) {
43	  const courses = await rows(tx, sql`select i.id item_id,i.slug,v.id version_id,v.version,v.title,v.body,v.fields,v.published_at from empower_content_versions v join empower_content_items i on i.id=v.item_id
44	    where i.kind='course' and v.status='published' and v.review_by >= ${UTC_TODAY} ${slug ? sql`and i.slug=${slug}` : sql``} order by v.title`)
45	  const lessonIds = [...new Set(courses.flatMap((c) => courseLessonIds(c.fields)))]
46	  const lessons = lessonIds.length ? await rows(tx, sql`select i.id item_id,i.slug,v.id version_id,v.version,v.title,v.body,v.fields,v.source_refs,v.published_at from empower_content_versions v join empower_content_items i on i.id=v.item_id
47	    where i.kind='lesson' and i.audience='partner_only' and v.status='published' and v.review_by >= ${UTC_TODAY} and i.id in (${uuidList(lessonIds)})`) : []
48	  const completions = await rows(tx, sql`select c.lesson_version_id,c.completed_at,v.item_id lesson_item_id from empower_academy_completions c join empower_content_versions v on v.id=c.lesson_version_id where c.partner_id=${partnerId}`)
49	  const states = await rows(tx, sql`select course_item_id,last_lesson_item_id,last_viewed_at from empower_academy_course_state where partner_id=${partnerId}`)
50	  const byLesson = new Map(lessons.map((l) => [String(l.item_id), l]))
51	  const views: CourseView[] = []
52	  for (const c of courses) {
53	    const fields = (c.fields ?? {}) as { category?: string; objectives?: string[]; modules?: CourseModule[]; estimated_minutes?: string }
54	    let completed = 0, available = 0, unavailable = 0, latest = new Date(String(c.published_at)).getTime(), minutes = 0, minutesKnown = true
55	    const modules = (fields.modules ?? []).map((m) => ({ title: m.title, ...(m.summary ? { summary: m.summary } : {}), lessons: m.lessons.map((id): LessonView => {
56	      const l = byLesson.get(id)
57	      if (!l) { unavailable++; return { itemId: id, available: false, state: "unavailable" } }
58	      available++
59	      const lf = (l.fields ?? {}) as { reading_minutes?: string; checks?: unknown[] }
60	      const done = completions.find((x) => String(x.lesson_version_id) === String(l.version_id))
61	      const earlier = !done && completions.some((x) => String(x.lesson_item_id) === id)
62	      if (done) completed++
63	      const reading = lf.reading_minutes ? Number(lf.reading_minutes) : null
64	      if (reading) minutes += reading; else minutesKnown = false
65	      latest = Math.max(latest, new Date(String(l.published_at)).getTime())
66	      return { itemId: id, available: true, versionId: String(l.version_id), version: Number(l.version), slug: String(l.slug), title: String(l.title), readingMinutes: reading, publishedAt: String(l.published_at),
67	        state: done ? "completed" : earlier ? "updated" : "not_started", completedAt: done ? String(done.completed_at) : null, checks: Array.isArray(lf.checks) ? lf.checks.length : 0 }
68	    }) }))
69	    if (!available) continue // fail closed: a course with no currently servable lesson is not offered at all
70	    const state = states.find((s) => String(s.course_item_id) === String(c.item_id))
71	    views.push({ itemId: String(c.item_id), slug: String(c.slug), versionId: String(c.version_id), version: Number(c.version), title: String(c.title), description: String(c.body), category: fields.category ?? null,
72	      objectives: fields.objectives ?? [], estimatedMinutes: fields.estimated_minutes ? Number(fields.estimated_minutes) : minutesKnown && minutes ? minutes : null, publishedAt: String(c.published_at), updatedAt: new Date(latest).toISOString(),
73	      modules, progress: { completed, available, unavailable }, lastLessonItemId: state ? String(state.last_lesson_item_id) : null, lastViewedAt: state ? String(state.last_viewed_at) : null })
74	  }
75	  return { views, byLesson }
76	}
77	
78	/** Dashboard and catalogue: every currently servable course with this partner's own progress. No lesson bodies. */
79	export async function getAcademy() {
80	  const actor = await partner()
81	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
82	    await tx.execute(sql`set transaction isolation level repeatable read`)
83	    const partnerId = await partnerGuard(tx, actor)
84	    const { views } = await load(tx, partnerId)
85	    const history = await rows(tx, sql`select count(*)::int n from empower_academy_completions where partner_id=${partnerId}`)
86	    return { enabled: true, courses: views, completionsRecorded: Number(history[0].n) }
87	  })
88	}
89	
90	/** One course with lesson bodies and knowledge-check questions (never answers or explanations before an attempt). */
91	export async function getAcademyCourse(input: { slug?: unknown }) {
92	  const actor = await partner()
93	  const slug = typeof input.slug === "string" && /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/.test(input.slug) && input.slug.length <= 120 ? input.slug : null
94	  if (!slug) throw new ContentError("Course not found.", 404)
95	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
96	    await tx.execute(sql`set transaction isolation level repeatable read`)
97	    const partnerId = await partnerGuard(tx, actor)
98	    const { views, byLesson } = await load(tx, partnerId, slug)
99	    const course = views[0]
100	    if (!course) throw new ContentError("This course is not available.", 404)
101	    const versionIds = course.modules.flatMap((m) => m.lessons.filter((l) => l.available).map((l) => l.versionId!))
102	    const attempts = versionIds.length ? await rows(tx, sql`select distinct on (lesson_version_id,question_id) lesson_version_id,question_id,correct,answer,attempted_at from empower_academy_check_attempts
103	      where partner_id=${partnerId} and lesson_version_id in (${uuidList(versionIds)}) order by lesson_version_id,question_id,attempted_at desc`) : []
104	    const lessons: Record<string, { body: string; sources: unknown; checks: unknown[] }> = {}
105	    for (const m of course.modules) for (const l of m.lessons) {
106	      if (!l.available) continue
107	      const src = byLesson.get(l.itemId)!
108	      const fields = (src.fields ?? {}) as { checks?: unknown }
109	      const full = Array.isArray(fields.checks) ? fields.checks as { id: string; answer: string[]; explanation: string }[] : []
110	      lessons[l.itemId] = { body: String(src.body), sources: (src as Row).source_refs ?? [], checks: publicChecks(fields.checks).map((q) => {
111	        const last = attempts.find((a) => String(a.lesson_version_id) === l.versionId && a.question_id === q.id)
112	        const key = full.find((f) => f.id === q.id)
113	        return last ? { ...q, lastAttempt: { correct: last.correct === true, given: last.answer, answer: key?.answer ?? [], explanation: key?.explanation ?? "" } } : q
114	      }) }
115	    }
116	    const related = await relatedResourcesForLessons(tx, Object.keys(lessons))
117	    for (const id of Object.keys(lessons)) (lessons[id] as typeof lessons[string] & { related?: unknown }).related = related[id] ?? []
118	    return { course, lessons }
119	  })
120	}
121	
122	const translate = (error: unknown, fallback: string): never => {
123	  if (error instanceof ContentError) throw error
124	  const safe = translateDbError(error, fallback)
125	  if (safe) throw new ContentError(safe.message, safe.status)
126	  throw error
127	}
128	
129	/** Optional, voluntary and idempotent: pressing "complete" twice records one completion. Refused if the lesson is no longer available. */
130	export async function completeAcademyLesson(input: { courseVersionId?: unknown; lessonVersionId?: unknown }) {
131	  const actor = await partner(), courseVersionId = uuid(input.courseVersionId), lessonVersionId = uuid(input.lessonVersionId)
132	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
133	    const partnerId = await partnerGuard(tx, actor)
134	    try {
135	      const inserted = await rows(tx, sql`insert into empower_academy_completions(id,partner_id,course_version_id,lesson_version_id) values(${randomUUID()},${partnerId},${courseVersionId},${lessonVersionId})
136	        on conflict (partner_id,lesson_version_id) do nothing returning id`)
137	      return { completed: true, alreadyRecorded: inserted.length === 0 }
138	    } catch (error) { return translate(error, "This lesson is not currently available.") }
139	  })
140	}
141	
142	/** "Continue where you left off". Recorded only for a lesson that is currently servable in that course. */
143	export async function recordAcademyView(input: { courseVersionId?: unknown; lessonVersionId?: unknown }) {
144	  const actor = await partner(), courseVersionId = uuid(input.courseVersionId), lessonVersionId = uuid(input.lessonVersionId)
145	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
146	    const partnerId = await partnerGuard(tx, actor)
147	    const [ok] = await rows(tx, sql`select empower_academy_lesson_servable(${courseVersionId}::uuid,${lessonVersionId}::uuid) ok, (select item_id from empower_content_versions where id=${courseVersionId}) course_item,
148	      (select item_id from empower_content_versions where id=${lessonVersionId}) lesson_item`)
149	    if (!ok?.ok) throw new ContentError("This lesson is not currently available.", 409)
150	    await tx.execute(sql`insert into empower_academy_course_state(partner_id,course_item_id,last_lesson_item_id) values(${partnerId},${String(ok.course_item)},${String(ok.lesson_item)})
151	      on conflict (partner_id,course_item_id) do update set last_lesson_item_id=excluded.last_lesson_item_id,last_viewed_at=now()`)
152	    return { recorded: true }
153	  })
154	}
155	
156	/** Grades an optional knowledge-check answer on the server and returns feedback. Retries are allowed; every attempt is kept privately. */
157	export async function attemptAcademyCheck(input: { courseVersionId?: unknown; lessonVersionId?: unknown; questionId?: unknown; answer?: unknown }) {
158	  const actor = await partner(), courseVersionId = uuid(input.courseVersionId), lessonVersionId = uuid(input.lessonVersionId)
159	  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
160	    const partnerId = await partnerGuard(tx, actor)
161	    const [lesson] = await rows(tx, sql`select v.fields from empower_content_versions v where v.id=${lessonVersionId} and empower_academy_lesson_servable(${courseVersionId}::uuid,${lessonVersionId}::uuid)`)
162	    if (!lesson) throw new ContentError("This lesson is not currently available.", 409)
163	    const result = gradeCheck((lesson.fields as { checks?: unknown } | null)?.checks, input.questionId, input.answer)
164	    try {
165	      await tx.execute(sql`insert into empower_academy_check_attempts(id,partner_id,course_version_id,lesson_version_id,question_id,answer,correct)
166	        values(${randomUUID()},${partnerId},${courseVersionId},${lessonVersionId},${result.questionId},${JSON.stringify(result.given)}::jsonb,${result.correct})`)
167	    } catch (error) { return translate(error, "This lesson is not currently available.") }
168	    return result
169	  })
170	}
171	
172	/**
173	 * Operation Empower B1.6: the partner's own continue-learning pointers for their workspace overview. Read-only; the caller has already
174	 * resolved the partner through partnerGuard, and only servable courses and lessons are returned. Kept here so learning records stay
175	 * readable only by the Academy service.
176	 */
177	export async function continueLearningFor(tx: Executor, partnerId: string): Promise<{ courseTitle: string; lessonTitle: string; href: string }[]> {
178	  const found = (await tx.execute(sql`select ci.slug course_slug,cv.title course_title,s.last_lesson_item_id,lv.title lesson_title
179	    from empower_academy_course_state s join empower_content_items ci on ci.id=s.course_item_id
180	    join empower_content_versions cv on cv.item_id=ci.id and cv.status='published' and cv.review_by >= (now() at time zone 'UTC')::date
181	    join empower_content_versions lv on lv.item_id=s.last_lesson_item_id and lv.status='published' and lv.review_by >= (now() at time zone 'UTC')::date
182	    where s.partner_id=${partnerId} order by s.last_viewed_at desc limit 3`)).rows as Record<string, unknown>[]
183	  return found.map((c) => ({ courseTitle: String(c.course_title), lessonTitle: String(c.lesson_title), href: `/partner/academy/${String(c.course_slug)}?lesson=${String(c.last_lesson_item_id)}` }))
184	}

/*
 * Operation Empower B1.4: the partner Knowledge Base. OFF unless PARTNER_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ENABLED=true, independent of the other
 * switches. Partners search approved knowledge entries (published, in date) with deterministic PostgreSQL full-text search and the
 * founder-managed synonyms; an exact alias or question match always ranks first. Each entry gives the precise partner answer, the
 * client-safe explanation, its limitation, when to escalate and its sources. Nothing is generated and nothing is logged.
 */
type Row = Record<string, unknown>
type Executor = Pick<AdminDatabaseTransaction, "execute">
export { partnerKnowledgeEnabled }
const rows = async (tx: Executor, query: SQL): Promise<Row[]> => (await tx.execute(query)).rows as Row[]
const SERVABLE = sql`v.status='published' and v.review_by >= (now() at time zone 'UTC')::date`

async function partner() {
  if (!partnerKnowledgeEnabled()) throw new ContentError("The Knowledge Base is not available yet.", 404)
  return requireCapability("expansion.partner")
}
type Fields = { question?: string; answer?: string; client_explanation?: string; limitations?: string; escalation_required?: string; escalation_condition?: string; escalation_route?: string; aliases?: string[]; topic?: string }
const shape = (r: Row) => {
  const f = (r.fields ?? {}) as Fields
  const client = (f.client_explanation ?? "").trim()
  return {
    itemId: String(r.item_id), slug: String(r.slug), audience: String(r.audience), version: Number(r.version), title: String(r.title),

/*
 * Operation Empower B1.5: the partner objection-handling workspace. OFF unless PARTNER_OBJECTION_HANDLING_ENABLED=true, independent of
 * the other switches. Partners search approved objection responses (published, in review date) with the B1.3 full-text index and the
 * founder-managed synonyms; an exact concern or alternative-phrasing match always ranks first, then rank, then slug. Each response
 * keeps the client-safe line (the only text offered for copying) apart from the partner explanation, limitation and escalation.
 * Related resources, lessons and knowledge entries are shown only when they are themselves servable and their module is switched on.
 * Nothing is generated and nothing is logged.
 */
type Row = Record<string, unknown>
type Executor = Pick<AdminDatabaseTransaction, "execute">
export const partnerObjectionsEnabled = () => process.env.PARTNER_OBJECTION_HANDLING_ENABLED === "true"
const rows = async (tx: Executor, query: SQL): Promise<Row[]> => (await tx.execute(query)).rows as Row[]
/** Published and within its review date (UTC calendar day). `asOf` exists only so tests can check expiry deterministically, as servableContent does. */
const servable = (asOf?: string) => {
  if (asOf !== undefined && !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(asOf)) throw new ContentError("Invalid date.")
  return asOf ? sql`v.status='published' and v.review_by >= ${asOf}::date` : sql`v.status='published' and v.review_by >= (now() at time zone 'UTC')::date`
}
const ALIASES = sql`jsonb_array_elements_text(case when jsonb_typeof(v.fields->'aliases')='array' then v.fields->'aliases' else '[]'::jsonb end)`
